builder_plan.scenario: Profiling shows attention computation is a bottleneck in your self-hosted service.
builder_plan.change: Check the supported GPU, tensor shapes, and precision, then replace only the relevant kernel.
builder_plan.baseline: The existing kernel inside the same complete serving pipeline.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Numerical differences, end-to-end latency, throughput, and memory at realistic shapes.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Tile-Based Decompression in Compiled GPU Engines
summary: Replaces decompressed-column materialization in HBM with fused on-chip decompression inside compiled GPU kernels. Costs include integration into a compiler-based execution engine (Proteus) and kernel complexity for cooperative tile decompression. Can fail if the production engine lacks compiler infrastructure to fuse decompression with downstream operators, or if compression encodings do not match query access patterns.
rationale: The technique targets analytical GPU query engines rather than ML inference workloads, and adoption requires compiler-level integration that is impractical without the specific Proteus infrastructure or equivalent GPU query compilation stack.
technique: Compiler-Fused Tile Decompression for GPU Query Engines

claims.statement: Replaces decompressed-column materialization in HBM with fused on-chip decompression inside compiled GPU kernels. Costs include integration into a compiler-based execution engine (Proteus) and kernel complexity for cooperative tile decompression. Can fail if the production engine lacks compiler infrastructure to fuse decompression with downstream operators, or if compression encodings do not match query access patterns.
Reduces resident memory footprint by up to 4x and memory-bandwidth consumption by up to 6x while maintaining competitive query times against HeavyDB and Sirius.
